description: Captures files from a folder in a Microsoft OneDrive drive via the Microsoft Graph API and parses them into records.

transports.purpose: Enumerate and download DriveItems from a OneDrive drive. Reached exclusively over the Microsoft Graph REST API v1.0 (msgraph-sdk-go for listing; a hand-rolled http.Client GET for content).

credentialModes.name: Microsoft OAuth2 (client id + secret + refresh token)

continuity.notes: Nothing is created or held on the customer's side: the connector only issues read-only Graph GETs (children listings and /content downloads) and leaves no server-side object. All resumption state is client-side in the Flow checkpoint (minBound/maxBound/maxMod modification-time window plus the last path and record offset), so an arbitrarily long pause is safe -- a file modified while we are stopped carries a newer lastModifiedDateTime and is picked up on the next sweep. Two caveats, both inherent to modification-time polling rather than to a lease: (a) a file whose content changes without its lastModifiedDateTime advancing past minBound is never re-read; (b) deletions are never observed, so the collection is append/merge-only and tombstones are not emitted. With advanced.ascendingKeys=true, minBound is deliberately never advanced and resumption is by lexicographic path instead, which additionally means files written out of lexicographic order are skipped forever.

configFields.description: Regex (format: regex) matched against every full file path under the folder; non-matching files are skipped.

configFields.description: The drive to access. If empty, the connector resolves the authenticated user's default drive via /me/drive.

configFields.name: advanced.ascendingKeys
configFields.description: Declares files are written in ascending lexicographic order; switches resumption from the modification-time window to 'start listing at the last path seen'. Default false.

discovery.method: Graph children listing of the configured folder; Discover itself emits exactly one binding derived from the endpoint config (DiscoverRoot = config.path), not from an enumeration of the drive.
discovery.querySketch: GET /v1.0/drives/{driveId}/items/root:{path}:/children?$orderby=name  (used by check(); Discover returns a single binding named after the trimmed path)
excludes: objects with size == 0 (treated as folder placeholders)
paths not matching the matchKeys regex
paths outside this shard's key range (HW-hash range check)
parquet objects larger than 8 GB (must be staged to local disk to parse)

backfill.compression: auto (gzip | zip | zstd | none, or auto-detected)
backfill.listing: First sweep runs the identical code path as the incremental leg with state.minBound = zero time, so every file under the prefix whose lastModifiedDateTime is < maxBound is read. Depth-first recursive walk: GET /v1.0/drives/{driveId}/items/root:{folderPath}:/children?$orderby=name for the root folder, then one such call per folder encountered, pushed onto an explicit stack; folder entries are expanded rather than emitted. Within a folder, paging is handled by msgraphcore.PageIterator, which follows the response's @odata.nextLink URL verbatim (the connector never parses a token out of it).

incremental.compression: auto (gzip | zip | zstd | none, or auto-detected)
incremental.listing: Same recursive children walk as the backfill; the incremental filter is entirely client-side. Each sweep picks maxBound = now - 30s (Source.TimeHorizonDelta = -30s) and processes only objects with minBound < lastModifiedDateTime < maxBound. On finishing a sweep, minBound advances to maxMod (the largest modification time actually processed), not to maxBound. There is NO Microsoft Graph `delta` token anywhere in this connector, so no delta-token expiry to manage. Mid-sweep resumption uses filesource.Query.StartAt = state.Path: the listing skips items lexicographically before StartAt unless the item path is a prefix of StartAt (so ancestor folders are still descended into), and per-file resumption skips state.Records already-emitted parsed records. When advanced.ascendingKeys is true, minBound is never advanced and StartAt alone drives resumption.

authTierRationale: Only one credential mode exists and its JSON schema requires all three of client_id, client_secret and refresh_token; credentials.validate() errors if any is empty. There is no app-password, device-code, client-credentials or certificate alternative, so standalone the user must register their own Azure app AND obtain a refresh token = T3. Estuary's hosted control plane mitigates this: the config carries "x-oauth2-provider": "microsoft" and main.go ships a pf.OAuth2 spec (authorization_code exchange against login.microsoftonline.com/common, scopes Files.Read.All offline_access User.Read, refresh_token plucked from /refresh_token of the token response), so in Estuary's UI the user just clicks through consent. That hosted flow is a control-plane feature, not something the connector binary provides; the standalone tier is T3_BYO_REFRESH. Note the connector itself only ever performs the refresh_token grant (an oauth2.Config TokenSource seeded with a pre-expired token), never the authorization_code leg.

unionMisfits.description: `objectStore` has no place for the fact that this store is a REST API with its own base URL, API version pinning and paginator. Everything goes through https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0 (path-segment version pinning), listings are @odata.nextLink-paginated, and content is a plain GET with an `Authorization: Bearer` header. Modelling it as `kind: "http"` would be equally wrong because there are no per-stream paths. The paginator, in particular, has nowhere to live: PullSpec `objects` has only a free-text `listing` field.

backfill and incremental are not two pull shapes here -- they are literally the same code with state.minBound either zero or carried forward. Filling both duplicates the spec; nulling backfill would hide that an initial full sweep happens. A `sameAsIncremental: true` marker (or a single `sweep` slot with a `firstRunBound` note) would express it honestly.

The connector has no schedule of any kind. filesource.Pull performs exactly one sweep per binding and returns; re-invocation cadence is entirely the Flow runtime's decision and is not encoded in the connector. `schedules: []` reads as 'not yet determined' rather than 'externally driven, by design'.

proposedShape.description: one bounded sweep per connector invocation; cadence owned by the orchestrator

unionMisfits.description: The cursor is a property of the OBJECT (DriveItem.lastModifiedDateTime), not a field of any emitted record -- emitted documents only contain the parsed file contents plus /_meta/file and /_meta/offset. A consumer reading cursorField as a record field would find nothing there. The real resumption state is a triple (minBound, maxBound, maxMod) plus a (path, records) position, which no single cursorField can carry.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: There is no schedule in the connector. filesource.Pull (filesource/filesource.go:336-376) runs exactly one sweep per binding and returns; nothing loops or sleeps. Cadence is imposed by whatever re-invokes the connector.
abstained.streams[0].schedules: Same reason as execution.defaultSchedule -- deliberately empty, not unknown. See unionMisfits[2].
abstained.streams[0].pull.incremental.listing:pagi: msgraphcore.NextPageIterator is an external dependency (github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-go-core) and is not vendored in this checkout, so its @odata.nextLink handling was not read first-hand. The connector passes the first page plus the request adapter to the iterator and never touches a token itself (main.go:169-187), which rules out token extraction on the connector's side; verbatim next-link following is the documented SDK behaviour but was inferred, not verified from source.
abstained.streams[0].writeDisposition: Rated medium rather than asserted: the key is (/_meta/file, /_meta/offset) so a re-read of a modified file overwrites the same keys (merge-like), but the connector emits no deletes and the runtime's reduction is a collection-schema property outside the connector. It is definitely NOT snapshot_with_tombstone.
abstained.streamMode: Rated medium: Discover always returns exactly ONE binding, named from the user's `path`. That is neither a shipped static list nor an enumeration of the customer's namespace. Recorded as 'discovered' because the stream name originates from customer config, but a reader should understand there is only ever one binding per capture.
abstained.transports[0].spec.store: The enum offers both 'drive' and 'sharepoint'. 'drive' was chosen for OneDrive; note that source-sharepoint uses the byte-identical Graph /drives/{id}/items API, so the two enum members do not actually distinguish different protocols.
